lots.guide_summary: All evidence is Gowans hammer prices in AUD (no conversion). Close same-type pile chobis of 4 to 7.4 sq m sold $330 to $630 hammer (4 sales, Aug to Sep 2026); smaller chobis $360 to $600. Three unsold (passed in) results, two of which sold on relist, and a same-size veg-dye chobi that passed in with 7 bids. No asking prices. Kilim and other rug types kept as category guides only.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-type sale of comparable size is $330 hammer (245x165, listed 2026-08-16). 330 / 1.198 = 275.5, rounded down to $275 hammer ($329 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $450 (middle of the $330 to $630 close sales), less 15% selling fees (auction seller commission) = $382.50, no postage (local pickup resale). 382.50 / 2.396 = 159.6, rounded down to $155. Recent large chobis have hammered at $330 or more, so a flip is unlikely to win; this is a keep-for-use lot.
lots.confidence_reason: Several opened Gowans sales of the same type and similar size, but only one photo, the front only; the rug number tag is not readable in the photo (only the 437 lot tag), and the back, pile depth and any moth or repairs cannot be seen. The Suzani design is less traditional, which could cut either way with buyers.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 12 researcher entries matched the API (title, size, rug no, hammer, bid count and listed date). Reclassified: the CHOBI KILIM $230 from close to category guide (flatweave, not pile). Added three UNSOLD results the researcher left out.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo, front only, hung on a rack. Cream/wheat ground, charcoal ikat-style zigzag lattice, three gold and red rosette medallions in hearts and three red heart cartouches with gold scrolls, small multicoloured star rosettes. Suzani-type design, not Ziegler. Colours look clean and even, no visible stains or holes on the front; the bottom fringe looks short and intact. Lot tag 437 visible.
lots.condition: Looks clean and bright from the front. Back, pile wear, moth, repairs and the other end's fringe not visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm lot 437 is hand-knotted wool pile (not a flatweave), and check the back and edges for moth, repairs, stains or worn pile and the condition of both fringes?

lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 9 researcher entries matched the API. Reclassified the $50 reeded-leg sale as close but poorer condition (excluded from maximum bids) after checking its photos. Added one UNSOLD (passed in three times). Corrected the researcher's 'possibly a later reproduction': the brass cup castors with ceramic wheels, carved leg blocks and moulded rounded top all look period.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Rounded-corner moulded top in strongly figured red timber, good polish with light scratches and a visible join to the inserted leaf (brass leaf-pin plate visible at the join). Carved floral blocks at the leg tops, ring-turned collars, reeded tapering legs, brass cup castors with white ceramic wheels (cropped and enlarged). No maker's mark visible. Timber looks more like mahogany than cedar from the figure.
lots.condition: Top polished with light surface wear; legs and castors look sound. Underside, winding mechanism and leaf condition unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: For lot 447, is the timber cedar or mahogany, does it extend with a winder (and is the handle included), does the single leaf match in colour and fit, and are there any loose joints or repairs to the legs?
